overview.description: Egyptian Ratscrew (ERS) is a high-energy, reflex-based card game combining War-style card playing with a social 'slapping' mechanic. Players take turns playing one card face-up to a central pile; when specific combinations appear (pairs, sandwiches, sequences, top-bottom matches, etc.), all players race to slap the pile. The fastest player takes all the pile's cards. The goal is to collect all 52 cards.

history.origins: Egyptian Ratscrew is a 20th-century American game derived from the British game Egyptian Rat Pack and the classic Slapjack. The 'Egyptian' name may be a humorous Americanism unrelated to Egypt.
timeline: Pre-1900s: Slapjack played in UK and USA.
Mid-1900s: Egyptian Rat Pack documented in UK.
Late 1900s: Egyptian Ratscrew codified in American college culture.
Present: One of the most popular casual card games among teenagers and college students.
history.evolution: The addition of multiple 'legal slap' conditions beyond simple Jack matching (sandwiches, doubles, marriages, sequences, etc.) gives ERS far more action and house-rule flexibility than Slapjack.
history.cultural: A staple of American teenage and college card culture. Known for the physical drama of slapping - and the painful penalty for false slaps.

setup.players: Two or more players; typically 2 to 7. The number of players is limited only by each participant's ability to reach the central pile. Cards are dealt as evenly as possible.
setup.dealing: Deal entire deck evenly. Players do not look at their cards; hold them face-down.

rules.objective: Collect all 52 cards by winning the central pile through valid slaps (on doubles, sandwiches, sequences, etc.) and by claiming the pile when opponents fail to counter face-card challenges.
rules.gameplay:
Players take turns playing one card face-up to the center pile. When a face card or Ace is played, the next player must play a face card within a set number of turns or forfeit their pile to the face-card player:
- Ace: 4 chances
- King: 3 chances
- Queen: 2 chances
- Jack: 1 chance
If they play a face card: the challenge passes forward.
keyRules: When a player runs out of cards, they may still slap back in.
If a player false-slaps and has fewer than 2 cards, they are eliminated.
Only designated slap conditions are valid (house rules vary widely).

strategy.basic: Stay alert at all timesâ€”doubles and sandwiches happen quickly. Don't pre-slap. Position your hand close to the pile without touching.
strategy.intermediate: Face Card Response: Know how many chances you have when challenged by a face card. Play your face cards carefullyâ€”an Ace buys you 4 attempts.
strategy.advanced: The fastest, most consistent slappers dominate. Memory helps: tracking the most recently played card greatly helps identify sandwiches and doubles before the card is even fully visible.
tips: Keep your eyes on the pile, not your cards.
If you're down to 2 cards, never false-slapâ€”elimination is instant.

deal.description: Deal entire deck evenly to all players. Cards remain face-down. Players do not look at their cards.
deal.constraints: Dealer acts during deal phase. All 52 cards dealt; hands held face-down.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands are played face-up during gameplay

award_pot.reason: No pot; pile taken by fastest slapper

play_card.description: Play top card from hand face-up onto pile.
play_card.constraints: When it is your turn in play order: play the top card from your face-down hand onto the center pile face-up. Players take turns clockwise until a slap condition occurs.

draw.reason: Cards dealt once; no drawing from stock

pass.reason: Players cannot pass; must play or slap

go_out.reason: Game ends when one player collects all cards

edgeCases.text: False slap: player must give one or more cards to bottom of pile; play resumes from last card.
Eliminated players (no cards) can slap in on a valid combination to rejoin while at least two players still have cards.
Face-card challenge: Ace gives 4 chances, King 3, Queen 2, Jack 1 for next player to play a face card or Ace; failure awards pile to challenger.
Cards played out of turn are dead; no valid slap on dead cards; penalty for slapping on dead card.
Contesting: if slap contested and legal, contesters give top card to slapper; if illegal, slapper gives one card to each challenger.
Players with no cards get strikes for false slaps; three strikes can remove slap ability or trigger burn-hands penalty (house rules vary).

engine.rankingSystem: Face cards (A,K,Q,J) trigger challenge. Rank comparison for slap conditions.
engine.deckDescription: Standard 52-card deck consisting of fifty-two cards in four suits, with thirteen ranks per suit from Ace to King; the entire deck is used and no jokers are required for play.
engine.suitDescription: French suit set: four suits—Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, and Clubs—each with thirteen cards, using the standard international symbols (♠ ♥ ♦ ♣).
engine.rankDescription: Standard fifty-two rank set: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, with thirteen cards in each suit; face cards and Aces trigger special slap or challenge rules.
